clue.text: Do remove the front of that festive headgear

parts.note: a do is informal British English for a party or celebration

indicators.note: tells us to drop the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: An instruction to snip the brim off a celebratory hat before a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like a verb but is the noun: a do is a party. Removing the front of 'that' leaves HAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper crown worn at celebrations is the classic festive item of headwear.

clue.text: Immature creature devoured in move towards adulthood

parts.note: a pup is a young animal, such as a young dog or seal
devoured means ate

explanation.surface: A young animal gets eaten as it grows up.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects turn into a pupa as a stage of development on the way to their mature form.

clue.text: Eritrea, unsettled after losing leading athlete, has to withdraw

indicators.note: unsettled suggests the letters are disturbed and rearranged
losing says a letter is taken away from the country's name
leading points to the first letter of the word athlete

explanation.surface: A runner from Eritrea, troubled after losing their top athlete, pulls out of competition.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the A (leading letter of 'athlete') from ERITREA to leave ERITRE, then 'unsettled' rearranges those six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To retire is to withdraw, as from a race, a job or a room.

clue.text: Returns and surrenders

definitions.meaning: investment returns are what it ... as profit
to surrender is to give way or concede

explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both producing a profit and giving way to another, so both senses match.

clue.text: It takes so long retrieve computer data from MCC — easiest altered

definitions.text: It takes so long retrieve computer data

indicators.note: altered signals that the letters given are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A grumble that data from the MCC, the cricket club, takes ages to fetch however you rearrange it.
explanation.walkthrough: MCC (Marylebone Cricket Club, the body behind English cricket's laws) plus EASIEST gives ten letters that 'altered' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: In computing, the delay between requesting data and receiving it is its retrieval time measurement.

clue.text: Compensate for inoperative company

parts.note: a machine that is inoperative is switched off
a set is a group or circle of people, as in the jet set

explanation.surface: A firm that has stopped working is asked to make amends.
explanation.definitionFit: To counterbalance or cancel out one thing with another is a standard synonym.

clue.text: Musicians cooking the books?

definitions.meaning: people who falsify accounts are said to fiddle them

explanation.definitionFit: Players of the violin and swindlers who falsify accounts share the same informal name.

clue.text: Leaves briefly with records secured by strapping

indicators.note: secured by means held inside the other word, which wraps round

parts.note: strapping means sturdy and well built, so stout
EPs are extended-play records

explanation.surface: Someone nips out for a while with a pile of vinyl tied up in straps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strapping' looks like a strap round the records but is the adjective meaning burly.
explanation.definitionFit: To go out for a short while, as from an office, is the phrasal verb meaning leaves for a moment.

clue.text: Adolescent has unwisely eaten half of burger

indicators.note: doing something unwisely means doing it wrongly, so the letters are jumbled
half of takes the back three letters of the six-letter word

explanation.surface: A youngster has foolishly scoffed half a burger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unwisely' rearranges EATEN into TEENA; the second half of BURGER is GER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone aged thirteen to nineteen is an adolescent, a young person in their teens.

clue.text: People being treated, say, with forbearance

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: people under medical treatment are patients

explanation.surface: Those under a doctor's care are said to show endurance.
explanation.definitionFit: Calm tolerance of delay or difficulty is forbearance, a close synonym.

clue.text: Stick the plug in this place

parts.note: a plug is an advertisement, shortened to ad
in this place means here

explanation.surface: An instruction to put the electric plug in here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plug' suggests a socket, but a plug is a piece of promotion: an AD.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to stick fast to a surface or to stick to a rule.

clue.text: Most drained one wine during trial

indicators.note: during means placed within the other word

parts.note: a trial is a test
one is the Roman numeral I
red is a kind of wine

explanation.surface: The person most exhausted had a glass of wine during a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: Drained means exhausted, so the most drained is the most weary.

clue.text: Al's map spoiled by some of the blood

indicators.note: spoiled indicates the letters are messed up and rearranged

parts.note: the letters of Al's taken with the s

explanation.surface: Someone's map has been ruined by a blood stain.
explanation.definitionFit: The pale liquid part of blood in which the cells are suspended forms part of it.

clue.text: Emphasise stress created by university at each introduction

parts.note: stress on a syllable is its accent

indicators.note: introduction points to the opening letter of the word each

explanation.surface: Lecturers make a point of stress caused by university life.
explanation.definitionFit: To accentuate something is to highlight or emphasise it.

clue.text: A neat way to go down under?

definitions.text: A neat way to go down under?

parts.words: A neat way to go down under?
parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, and down under is Australia, so a cattle-droving track in the outback

explanation.surface: A tidy route for travelling to Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' seems to mean tidy, but it is the old word for cattle, as in neatsfoot oil.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australia, a public track for droving cattle across country has this name.

clue.text: The resting place of many an old wreck?

definitions.text: The resting place of many an old wreck?

parts.words: The resting place of many an old wreck?
parts.note: an old wreck suggests a decrepit person laid to rest, but here it is a sunken ship on the sea floor

explanation.surface: Where worn-out old people finally lie down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wreck' and 'resting place' suggest a tired person and a bed or grave; the wreck is a ship on the sea floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunken ships lie on the floor of the sea, and the second word puns on a place for rest.

clue.text: We must have time to get nets in swampy areas

parts.note: taken as written
to net a fish is to land it

explanation.surface: A fishing party needs time to haul nets in the marshes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nets' looks like a noun but is the verb: catches, so LANDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Marshes, fens and swamps are classed as soggy terrain of this kind.

clue.text: Not moving, I'm with a crowd three quarters of a mile below

indicators.note: in a down answer, below means this piece comes after the others

parts.note: taken without the apostrophe
a mob is an unruly crowd

indicators.note: three quarters of a four-letter word means three of its letters, here the last three

explanation.surface: Someone stuck still in a crowd a little under a mile away.
explanation.definitionFit: Something immobile is stationary, not moving at all.

clue.text: One of the ship's company has a possible cut limb

parts.note: a crew cut is one possible hairstyle
a limb is a member of the body

explanation.surface: A sailor has an injured arm that might need cutting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut limb' reads as a wound, but 'a possible cut' is CREW (as in crew cut) and the limb is a MEMBER.
explanation.definitionFit: A person in a ship's company belongs to its staff of sailors.

clue.text: A sort of bread-and-scrape?

indicators.note: sort of here means a jumbled version of the following word

explanation.surface: A kind of thin bread and dripping snack.
explanation.walkthrough: Bread-and-scrape is a meagre slice with only a scraping of butter; here 'scrape' is the definition and 'sort of bread' rearranges BREAD.
explanation.definitionFit: To abrade is to scrape or wear away by rubbing.

clue.text: Road rage is an illusion!

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI in crosswords
taken as written

explanation.surface: A claim that road rage is only imagined.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; crosswords write its 1 as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Something illusory, such as water seen shimmering in the desert, is a mirage.

clue.text: Right? Redistribute seats around state

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters surround the other piece
redistribute means hand out again in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A call to reallocate parliamentary seats in a state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Redistribute' turns SEATS into ASSET, and 'around' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To state firmly is to assert or declare.

clue.text: Flowering lily initially planted in a time of rapid growth

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: planted in means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: a boom is a period of rapid economic growth

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of lily

explanation.surface: A lily, first planted during a surge in growth, comes into flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants that are in bloom are flowering.

clue.text: Filthy stalls containing poor bub's little bottles

indicators.note: containing means the outer word holds the other inside

parts.note: sties are dirty pens for pigs

indicators.note: poor signals a broken, rearranged version

parts.note: bub, informal for a young child; the possessive gives no letter

explanation.surface: Grimy stables house a poor baby's tiny feeding bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: Bub is American slang for a baby or young fellow; stubbies are Australian beer bottles. 'poor' rearranges BUB into UBB.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australia, short squat beer bottles are called stubbies.

clue.text: What President Coolidge was said to have done with liquor outlaw

indicators.note: said tells us to hear the phrase spoken

parts.note: Calvin Coolidge was US president during Prohibition, when alcohol was banned

explanation.surface: A trivia question about Coolidge's attitude to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Prohibition years Coolidge's government banned liquor: 'banned it' spoken sounds like the word for a robber.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandit is a robber or outlaw.

clue.text: A speed car comes first with a hard top

indicators.note: comes first with means this piece goes before the others

parts.note: taken as written
pace is speed

explanation.surface: A fast car leads the field with a hardtop roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A carapace is the hard upper shell of a crab or tortoise.

clue.text: Sprinter, the German, remains inside

indicators.note: inside means put within the other word

parts.note: der is German for the
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A German runner's remains are kept within.
explanation.definitionFit: A dasher is someone who dashes, a fast runner over a short distance.

clue.text: Dwelling for rival not finished, housed in temporary accommodation

indicators.note: housed in means placed inside the other word

parts.note: a tent is a temporary shelter

indicators.note: not finished means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: an enemy is an opponent or rival

explanation.surface: A rival is put up in a tent while a home is found.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenement is a dwelling, typically a rented flat in a large building.
